M4 delivers the terminal font family, font size and scrollback settings (stored in `settings.json`, edited in a "Terminal" section of the existing gear dialog, applied live) because its task "font and scrollback settings" needs somewhere to live. M6's settings dialog keeps theme and data folder and absorbs this section instead of building it; its task "terminal font and size, scrollback" is therefore already done when M6 starts. M4 also keeps russh's `rsa` feature (owner decision) and so ships with a time-boxed `deny.toml` ignore for `RUSTSEC-2023-0071`, to be removed once russh depends on `rsa` 0.10.0 or later.

Three small additions that came up while building the tab area, none of them a later milestone's work. Double-clicking a folder in the tree expands or collapses it (a connection opens as before). The sidebar's gear dialog is titled "Settings" (it holds the terminal section planned above next to the data folder), which M6's settings dialog builds on. `ui/vite.config.ts` raises `build.chunkSizeWarningLimit` to 700 kB because the terminal stays in the main chunk on purpose (`Docs/DECISIONS.md`, "M4 terminal: xterm.js versions, WebGL policy, no lazy import"). Deferred to the backlog: confirming quit with live sessions, restoring tabs after a restart, native clipboard commands (needs a BSL-1.0 licence decision) and a separate timeout for agents that need a confirmation.

M5 supports mRemoteNG files of ConfVersion 2.6 only, which is what the stable 1.76 line writes (the owner runs it). The legacy AES-CBC format (below 2.6) is not cheap and stays in the backlog; the pre-release formats 2.7 and 2.8 (credentials in a separate repository) are refused with a clear message. The first check on the owner's sanitised fixture is its `ConfVersion`: if it is not 2.6 the work stops and this entry is revised. Restore semantics (owner decision): a full backup replaces tree and vault entries after a confirmation, the connections-only JSON merges into a new top-level folder. M5 also adds small primitives to `fernjo-core` and `fernjo-vault` (graft and replace tree, password-sealed blob, add, export and replace entries) and a debug-build-only `FERNJO_DIALOG_FILE` override for the native file dialogs, so the flows can be checked without OS input.

Owner request: M6 ends with a release-readiness and security check, so the milestone is renamed "Packaging, app settings & release readiness" and gains two tasks (a security audit of the release candidate and a release-readiness gate that prepares v0.1.0 without releasing it) and two acceptance criteria (security review without an open High finding; a go/no-go verdict with every known gap named in `Docs/release-checklist.md`). Three more additions belong to the same goal and are not later milestones' work: third-party licence notices inside the installers (shipping MIT, Apache, OFL and MPL dependencies in binaries needs them), installer smoke tests in the release workflow (an installer that was never installed proves little), and a dry run of the release workflow on pull requests (`workflow_dispatch` only exists once the file is on the default branch `dev`). The four settings-dialog follow-ups parked in the backlog ("Saved" stays after editing, async load overwrites typing, failed load leaves empty fields, no IME check) are fixed because M6 rebuilds that dialog. Open decision carried into the milestone: if the measured idle memory misses the spec's ~150 MB, the target or its definition moves only with the owner's answer, recorded here. The attach step of the release workflow can only be rehearsed against a real (draft) release after the pull request is on `dev`; creating it needs the owner's go-ahead.

Work added to M6 during execution, all in service of the security review task: the independent crate reviews of vault, SSH and import and a `/security-review` of the milestone diff (findings and dispositions in `Docs/release-checklist.md`), and the fixes that came out of them. Import limits for hostile mRemoteNG files (XML attribute and namespace scan, string length caps; `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, "M6 security review: import limits"); the tree depth limit enforced on every create, move and duplicate (`too_deep`); a 64 MiB cap on reading `vault.fernjo` and host name validation before `known_hosts` writes (`invalid_host`; "M6 security review: vault file size cap and known_hosts host validation"); plain `ssh-rsa` no longer offered, with the exact algorithm lists pinned by a test ("M6 security review: SSH algorithm policy"); russh 0.65.2 and rsa 0.10.0, so the `RUSTSEC-2023-0071` ignore is gone ("M6 security review: RUSTSEC-2023-0071 ignore removed"); owner-only file modes 0600 and 0700 on Unix ("M6 security review: data files are owner-only on Unix"). The performance task also produced measurement tooling (`tools/measure-performance.ps1`, `tools/perf/cdp.mjs`, results in `Docs/performance.md`; "M6 performance measurements: definitions and results"), and the installer smoke tests are recorded in "M6 installer smoke tests: what they prove and where they run". Findings left to the owner or to the backlog are in the block "Open manual checks (owner)" and the backlog.

After the security review the owner decided to fix four findings before v0.1.0 instead of accepting or deferring them: (1) the navigation guard on the main webview (finding 4, was backlog; remote origins are refused, WebView2 still sends one blind GET for a cancelled top-level GET navigation, so the risk is reduced, not closed); (2) vault rollback protection with a generation counter and per-device marks, including 'Open the older vault' (finding 14); (3) auto-unlock never deletes the keychain item and the unlock note says why it did not work (finding 15); (4) hosts in the synced `known_hosts` that this device has not confirmed ask once per device (finding 16, replaces the earlier 'document only' decision). Each existing `known_hosts` host asks once per device after the update; accepting an older vault re-stamps it at once. A device-local folder outside the synced data folder (`<OS local data dir>/fernjo-device`) holds the marks and the confirmed hosts. Plan: `superpowers/plans/2026-11-18-milestone-06-security-fixes.md`; decisions: `DECISIONS.md` entries 'M6 security fixes: device-local folder', 'vault rollback protection', 'hosts confirmed on this device', 'Vault: keychain behaviour' and the navigation guard update. The navigation guard backlog entry is removed.

backlog.title: M4 review follow-ups
backlog.text:
Deferred from the whole-branch review of M4, none of them blocks the milestone:

- `SshError` carries no source (thin diagnostics); the error mapping is coarse and `io_to_lost` is misnamed.
- `known_hosts`: the BOM is lost when the first line is replaced; a duplicate host inside one entry's host list leaves a stale entry; test gaps (hashed non-22 and IPv6 hosts, tab separators, add on a CRLF file).
- `TrustAlways` and `Replace` write `known_hosts` before the key-exchange signature is verified; park the decision and write after `connect_stream` succeeds.
- A russh session task and its file descriptor leak on a pre-key-exchange timeout.
- The session input queue is unbounded; cap it (about 8 MiB).
- `tauri_plugin_opener::init()` injects an init script; use `Builder::new().open_js_links_on_click(false).build()`.
- The agent test is named "in order" but asserts only that the login works.
- Chords use `e.key` instead of `e.code`, so Ctrl+Shift chords fail on non-Latin layouts.
- Terminal: the `ResizeObserver` is not coalesced per frame, `findNext` is not incremental, the search bar hardcodes 13 px.
- Tabs: an Escape-cancelled drag still fires a click; arrow keys fire from the Close and Reconnect buttons and there is no Home, End or Delete; the tab ARIA is loose; `.reconnect` uses weight 500 where `DESIGN.md` says 400; the lock icon is 12 px inside a 10 px mark; `protocolOf` could be `Tab.protocol`.
- Ctrl+Shift+W with the vault view open closes an invisible tab.
- Prompts: a keyboard-interactive round with zero prompts has no focus target; the needs-vault busy flag resets before the resume (double click); `PasswordField` `shown` is not reset after a wrong password; the `FOCUSABLE` selector omits `textarea` and `select`.

backlog.title: connections.json lost update when a sync tool delivers a newer file
backlog.text: The app keeps the tree in memory and rewrites `connections.json` on every change, so a file that Syncthing, Nextcloud or Dropbox delivers while the app runs is overwritten and the other device's edits are lost. The vault already guards against this (M3: `Vault::save` re-reads the file and refuses with `changed_on_disk` unless it still starts with the header the handle last read or wrote). Apply the same check-then-write idea to the tree: remember a fingerprint (for example a hash or the length and modification time) of the last bytes read or written, compare it before saving, and refuse or offer to reload when the file changed. It stays a check, not a lock, so a sync tool can still win the race between check and rename.

backlog.title: What is the WebView2 background connection?
backlog.text: From M6 security review finding 5. About 60 s after start the Windows WebView2 runtime (not fernjo.exe) opens one HTTPS connection to an address registered to Microsoft; its purpose is not verified and `--disable-background-networking` did not stop it. Find out what it is and whether a WebView2 setting turns it off; check macOS and Linux too. The README privacy statement says what is known today.

backlog.title: Remove build paths from release binaries
backlog.text: From M6 security review finding 6. CI-built binaries embed the runner's cargo registry paths in panic locations (`C:\Users\runneradmin\.cargo\registry\...`, `/home/runner/.cargo/...`, `/Users/runner/.cargo/...`); no personal name occurs in any installer. Set `RUSTFLAGS=--remap-path-prefix` in `release.yml` if the paths should disappear.

backlog.title: Dev-dependency alert: minimatch
backlog.text: From M6 security review finding 7. Dependabot alert for `minimatch` 10.2.6 (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249), a development dependency of typescript-eslint; `pnpm audit --prod` is clean. Take the update when typescript-eslint moves. The `glib` 0.18.5 alert (Tauri's GTK3 stack) is a known gap recorded in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` since M0; revisit when Tauri leaves GTK3.

backlog.title: Vault Low findings
backlog.text: From the M6 independent vault review (`Docs/release-checklist.md`, finding 17). Attacker-chosen KDF cost accepted at load (1 GiB, 20 passes, 16 lanes: about 15 s per unlock attempt; backups the same, 16.7 s); the temp file name is fixed, followed through symlinks, no `create_new`, no directory fsync; the Windows keychain item uses "Enterprise" persistence by default (credential roaming); secret residue in freed buffers (`normalise`, `save`, plain `[u8; 32]` copies, the argon2 matrix); `change_password` never upgrades the KDF cost; the header is re-encoded from parsed fields (a trap when `CURRENT_VERSION` becomes 2); the public `Secret` derives `Serialize`. Related: `connections.json` and `settings.json` are read without a size cap.

backlog.title: SSH Low findings
backlog.text: From the M6 independent SSH review (`Docs/release-checklist.md`, finding 18). `known_hosts` `replace` removes only the first matching entry of a line, so a hand-edited `h,H` line leaves the old key trusted; a key of another algorithm for a stored host reads as a new host (a legitimate key-type rotation fails with a generic protocol error); `@revoked` lines are ignored (documented); `known_hosts` writes use a fixed temp name, no `create_new` and no cross-session lock; server keyboard-interactive text and prompt count are unbounded in the UI; secrets are copied into plain `String`s for the wire; no host key re-check on re-key (russh); Windows agent pipe squatting (same as OpenSSH for Windows).

backlog.title: Import and backup Low findings
backlog.text: From the M6 independent import review (`Docs/release-checklist.md`, finding 19). Unbounded attacker strings reach the webview in error messages and in backup `createdAt` and `app`; the export-target guard covers only the data folder (not the config folder or a pending data folder); names, hosts and descriptions of the JSON and backup import paths are not validated for control characters or length (the mRemoteNG path got length caps in M6); `import_apply` holds the pending lock across the disk work while the page-load hook takes it on the UI thread (a reload during a slow save freezes the window); residual unzeroised non-secret copies. A restored backup replaces the tree and the vault entries by design, so the confirmation could name more than counts.

backlog.title: M6 security fixes: deferred follow-ups
backlog.text:
From the M6 security fixes (plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-18-milestone-06-security-fixes.md`, reviews and `Docs/release-checklist.md` findings 4, 14, 16). None blocks v0.1.0.

- Concurrent host confirmations (two sessions confirming at once) may lose an update: the confirmed-hosts file is written through a fixed `.tmp` name without a lock (fails safe: the host asks again).
- Vault rollback: two histories that reach the same generation (an equal-generation divergence) are not detected.
- A startup notice when `settings.json` holds a `dataDir` that contains the device-local folder (the folder dialog refuses it, a hand-edited `settings.json` does not).
- A host key of another type for a host the device confirmed earlier (a key-type downgrade) shows no `previous` fingerprint in the prompt.
- `Unknown` plus 'trust always' does not replace a different key of the same type in the confirmed-hosts file.

backlog.title: Close the tab when the shell exits on purpose
backlog.text:
Owner request of 2026-11-18, reported while testing on macOS; for after v0.1.0 (the owner decided that this and the two items above come after the first release). It applies on all platforms. Today a session tab turns yellow ('connection lost', Reconnect) also when the user ends the shell on purpose, for example with `exit`, `logout` or Ctrl+D in a Linux terminal. Wanted: the tab closes itself after an intentional end, but stays yellow with Reconnect when the connection drops.

Design notes: the SSH server reports a deliberate shell end as a channel exit-status (or exit-signal) followed by EOF and close, whereas network loss, a keepalive timeout, a reset or a transport error carries no exit status. Rule: auto-close only for a clean exit-status; keep the tab for transport errors, timeouts and server-side disconnect messages that have an error reason. Exceptions so that nothing disappears unread: a session that ends within the first few seconds after login (for example 'Permission denied' or an error banner) stays open, and optionally a non-zero exit status stays open too. A setting 'Close the tab when the shell exits' in Settings (suggested default on, switchable off, remembered like the terminal settings in `settings.json` with the existing persistence rules). It touches the SSH session end handling in `fernjo-ssh`, the session manager (`sessions.rs`: the end-of-session event gets an `exitStatus` or 'ended cleanly' field in the wire contract described at the top of that file, rationale in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` 'M4 session IPC') and the tab logic in the UI. Tests for each ending kind; the SSH container tests (`tools/ssh-test-server.sh`) can produce `exit 0`, `exit 3` and a killed connection.

backlog.title: Linux title bar icon placeholder
backlog.text:
Owner observation of 2026-11-18 on a CachyOS (Arch) laptop with the AppImage (`Docs/release-checklist.md` gap 27, Low, cosmetic): the title bar of the window shows a placeholder logo instead of the fernjo icon, while the icon in the Linux taskbar is correct. For after v0.1.0 unless the diagnostics below point to a cheap fix.

Established by the controller: `tauri-codegen` embeds as the default window icon on Linux the first `.png` of `bundle.icon` in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, which is `icons/32x32.png`, and that file is the correct fernjo icon (charcoal tile, ring, yellow dot), so the embedded window icon is right. Probable cause, not verified: the compositor looks the title bar icon up through the app id (identifier `io.github.benjo-code.fernjo`) in a `.desktop` file, which an AppImage run without desktop integration does not provide; the taskbar showing the right icon points to a different lookup.

Diagnostics for the owner: note the desktop environment and session type (Wayland or X11); run `GDK_BACKEND=x11 ./fernjo_0.0.0_amd64.AppImage` (if the title bar icon is right under X11, it is the Wayland app-id lookup); try an integrated AppImage (Gear Lever or AppImageLauncher; if it is right after integration, it is the missing desktop file of an unintegrated AppImage). Possible fixes: set the window icon explicitly in `setup` with `tauri::include_image!` and `set_icon`, or ship a `.desktop` file with the AppImage that matches the app id. If the cause is confirmed as an environment limit, add a known-limits sentence to the README.

backlog.title: Discoverability and clarity of the UI (review of the whole app)
backlog.text:
Owner request of 2026-11-18, found while testing the first installed builds; for after v0.1.0. It applies on all platforms. It is related to, but separate from, the other post-v0.1.0 UI items (resizable panels, multi-select in the tree, close the tab on an intentional shell exit). The owner did not immediately find where Import/Export and Settings are, and above all did not realise that the sidebar chip showing only 'unlocked' and a padlock is the credential vault, where logins (credentials) are defined. If the owner, who knows the app, did not see it, new users will not either.

Wanted:

- Make the vault recognisable and self-explanatory: a label that says 'Vault' or what it holds, a short explanation or first-run hint for 'where do I store logins', clear locked and unlocked wording, and an obvious path from a connection's 'Credential' property to the vault manager.
- Make Import & backup, Export and Settings easier to find and name consistently (the sidebar footer today: a gear for Settings and 'Import & backup').
- A general review of the whole app for clarity: labels, empty states, first-run guidance, icons that come with text, the wording of the properties panel, discoverability of context menus, keyboard shortcuts and the session and tab actions, and confusing states (locked vault, host key prompts).

Approach: do it as a design critique with real screenshots (the `impeccable` skill; `DESIGN.md` and the tokens in `ui/src/styles/tokens.css` apply, no new visual direction), turn the findings into a short list, agree it with the owner, then implement the agreed changes with tests.
